items.note: S1.3.2 states the outcome (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with restoration of arbitrary scratch, and S1.3.1 names the gates and the intersection-size coefficients; but the per-invocation effect y_S <- y_S + x_S, the eight-row schedule and the forward/inverse/forward pattern of the stages are not stated, and S1.3.1 has the side and central wires jointly 'cancel' coefficients, whereas the central wires produce them and the side wires cancel them (lines 752-758).

S1.3.3 gives an invertible frame at each vertex, the commutation of a common frame with pointwise linear gates, and the identity D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, as at lines 804-829. It leaves out the edge operator D_v D_u^{-1} and the per-route form epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, and gives no sub-derivation.

S1.3.4a restates the lemma's first claim correctly (comparable nondegenerate labels; only the central-wire edges decrease, each by h). The triple-indicator labels and their orthogonality, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L and L<N/2 (100/539, 101/539) are absent. The method names the route, but no sub-step shows how the lemma is obtained.

S1.3.4b gives the bit-network rank sum s=Wm-N+2L<Wm, quoting line 1146, but presents it for a generic network. The projection matrices, the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and the resulting shear H<-H+D on every role are not stated, and nothing justifies the 'therefore' (N-2L>0).

S1.5.0 says the frame changes are products of kernels aI+bX_v that telescope to C^{tensor m} on every role. It omits that there is one kernel (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, the count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, and the diagonal corrections and undoing of the signed exchange that the telescoping needs (lines 1225-1227, 1298-1315).

The plan states s<Wm and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, and quotes that both deficits exceed 20*2^{-50} (line 1331). The deficit values eta_b and eta_c, the step log m<20 and the cause L<N/2 are missing, and the complex inequality (s_c/W_c<m^sigma) is not stated separately.

S1.1 matches Lemma lem:elementary-streams. S1.2 drops the condition that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time and the prime modulus, and presents multiplication by fixed units as a consequence of the shift ('which also multiplies'), whereas the lemma states it as a separate O(V) operation (lines 569-570).

S1.4.1 and S1.4.2 state both lemmas faithfully (E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones; exactly a interchanges of b-digit fields plus O(V)). How each one of Pi becomes one interchange (lines 1436-1441) and the choice of a fixed prime are not shown.

The route is there: frames, edge shears by rank-many recursive interchanges, s calls on volume V/W, and F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with s/W<m^tau, giving O(Ve^tau). Three things are missing: the cyclic split of rows into W role streams, which needs the row field divisible by W^k ('enough rows' is loose); the shear H<-H+D on every row; and its conversion to an interchange by D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D (lines 1534-1540). The fixed-tape schedule is not mentioned.

S1.4.4 states the address permutation (p,h,g,d,z)->(p,d,g,h,z) in O(Vu^tau), as in Lemma lem:chunk-swap. The method only says 'remove the width and row restrictions', with no padding or base-m decomposition.

S1.5's method names expressing C^{tensor} through phase frames, binary basis changes and conversion to the normalized layer, without content: no P_M conjugation, no s_c child calls of C^{tensor f}, no inverse identity and no H_0=bSCS.

S1.5.1 describes whole-chunk cyclic shifts, repair of a bounded exceptional set and a restored third chunk. The positions j_i=rho+iK, the count of eight shifts, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}} and the time bound O(V(L^tau+1)) are missing.

The layer's recurrence appears only through S1.5's dependence on the generic recursion of S1.3/S1.3.5, whose O(1) overhead is not the layer's O((eK)^tau+1). The rows taken from the first q_0 chunks, the cutoff at e<d^beta and the summation to d^{lambda'} are absent.

The plan states the layer H_0 on one selected bit per chunk for up to d chunks of polynomial records, returned as Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}, evaluated exactly before one truncation, as in Prop. prop:simultaneous-layer. The guard width Delta and the depth bound are not given.

S2.1 gives the layout (selected bits at a common offset in K-bit chunks), the cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]) and a fixed frequency order. It omits character cancellation (F^+F^-=t^{-1}I), bit-reversed order, the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, and the error bound.

S2.2 states exact multiplication by signed Kronecker packing into four integer products, then division by r and truncation. It omits the evaluation point 2^{4p} and the cost O(rp log(rp)), the cost row this lemma supplies.

The route is the paper's: two forward transforms kept in a common order, pointwise packed products, the opposite transform on that order, and the error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} (S2.3). S2's cost omits the +log(rp) term of the proposition. The commutation P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), the normalization identity and the final exact scaling by M are missing.

S3.1.1 and S3.1.2 state both lemmas accurately: conditions, P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, error and time, the tensor identity and the exposure cost. The construction of A and B_0 (lines 3576-3792) is not shown; the only derivation is that tensoring follows from the one-axis case.

S3.2 states that R cancels to (u*v)/S^2 and that QF_t becomes a Bluestein chirp convolution. The chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i), the identity QF_t u = abar.(a*(abar.u))/T and the conjugation rule for RF^+ are missing.

The prime window (1-2eta)t_i<s_i<=(1-eta)t_i with T/2<S<T, and the sizes p=6ceil(log n), d~p^epsilon, T~n/log n, are given. The fixed exponent values (only kappa and tau are given), eta=1/(4d), alpha, gamma=o(b), t_i in {r/2,r} and the existence argument for the primes are missing.

S3.4 states that Phi is a CRT map preserving cyclic convolution and is implemented by triangular controlled shifts, as in the paper. The definition x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i}a_jP_j and the cost are not given.

S3.5 gives the twist by zeta^k with zeta=e^{pi i/r}, which turns a length-r cyclic convolution into one modulo y^r+1, with untwisting restoring the wrap; this matches lines 4302-4319. The resulting M_C formula and the twist error are not stated.

The plan states the source-transform composition (A, chirp, B_0, scale 2^gamma, conjugation for the opposite sign) and the six steps. It omits the exact counterpart RF_s and the digit scaling, and 'rescales twice by S' drops the factor 2^{2b+4} of the second scale (line 4522).

S3.8 gives the conclusion: total error below 1/2, then rounding and carries give the exact product. It gives none of the bounds (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-3b/4}) and does not say that gamma<=b/4 and p=6b are what make the error small.

The route is the paper's: costs over Tp written as powers of p, margins g_1..g_7 with minimum 2^{-181}=2kappa, the bound O(Tp p^{1-kappa}) and schoolbook below a cutoff. The rows of the table, the identity of the binding margin g_2=epsilon c(1-tau), the absorption of log factors into p^kappa and the o(V) setup are not given.
Only the dependency tag 'nlogn-conjecture' on S0 alludes to the conjecture. No step says how the bound refutes an eventual n lg n lower bound (liminf zero), so the conservative verdict is absent.

errors.says: The generic recursion from the fixed network has cost per volume F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1); S1.5 inherits it for the butterfly layer through 'recursive-power-saving'.
errors.paper: That recurrence (eq:swap-recurrence) is the interchange's. The layer's recurrence has node overhead O((eK)^tau+1), leaves F(e)=O(e) for e<d^beta, and exponent lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}, not sigma.

errors.says: The sum s of the rational ranks of the edge differences is Wm-N+2L, presented for the generic network used by both procedures.
errors.paper: Wm-N+2L is the bit network's rational rank sum s_b. The complex network's count is the sum of orthonormal basis lengths, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c.
Prop. prop:synthetic-convolution has cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}+log(rp)]); the log(rp) term from the M packed products is a separate row of the cost table.

errors.says: Auxiliary side and center wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.
errors.paper: The central wires carry the main coefficient (|S∩T| mod 2, or (|S∩T|-1)/2), and only the side injection cancels the unwanted neighbour coefficients.

errors.says: The algorithm rescales twice by S.
errors.paper: Step 4 multiplies by S; step 5 multiplies by 2^{2b+4}S before rounding.

errors.says: A controlled shift 'also multiplies a field by fixed units modulo q^b'.
errors.paper: Multiplication by specified rational units is a separate O(V) operation of the lemma, not a by-product of the shift; the shift also requires an offset preparable in b^{O(1)} time.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route: scalar exchange network, frames, subspace labels with s<Wm, matrix shears, power-width then arbitrary-width interchange, the phase interface and packed additions for the layer, synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling with retained permutations, chirp cancellation, the CRT map, the twist, exact recovery and the cost margins. It is thin at the core saving: L<N/2, the shear endpoint identity and the shear-to-interchange conversion are missing, and the layer's own recursion (s_c children via P_M conjugation, overhead O((eK)^tau+1), cutoff at d^beta) is replaced by a generic O(1)-overhead recurrence. Later, most steps are quoted statements, not derivations.
